overview: White plays 2.b4 against the French, offering the pawn to deflect the bishop and open the queenside. After 2...Bxb4 White can play 3.e5 (Pinova Gambit) or 3.Bb2 with a lead in development. Black can usually keep the pawn with accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Use Bb2 and d4 for a quick centre
Push e5 and develop with tempo

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...Bxb4 and develop sensibly
Return it only when it helps neutralise the attack

character.notes: A pawn offer by White at move two makes the game concrete.

gambit.notes: 2.b4 Bxb4 leaves Black a pawn up that is hard to win back.

structure.notes: After 3.e5 the centre is French-like and closed.

approach.notes: Strong players do not play 2.b4 against the French.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pinova Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: White gains space and gives a pawn for kingside play.

character.reason: A queenside pawn offer with quick development leads to concrete play.

gambit.reason: White gives the b-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Strong players consider 2.b4 an unsound surprise.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided between open and French-closed.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly choose 2.b4 against the French.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White gives a pawn for time and space.
